feedback_text: The instructor made programming concepts very intuitive with live coding demonstrations. Truly enjoyed this class.
The homework assignments were clear and helped prepare us well for the quizzes.
Slides had way too much code crammed onto a single page and the pacing was hard to follow.
Great introductory course! Office hours were always welcoming and patient.
The transition from Python basics to object-oriented programming was very confusing and rushed.
Loved the hands-on mini-projects. It gave me confidence in writing clean code.
Teaching assistants were super helpful during the weekly laboratory sessions.
I struggled to understand recursion because the lecture examples were too abstract.
Explanations of graph algorithms and dynamic programming were lucid and thorough.
The project specifications were vague and contradicted what the teaching assistant told us.
Having two massive coding assignments due during midterm week was overwhelming and caused extreme stress.
The professor reads off bullet points monotonically for two hours without interactive discussions.
Grading was delayed by six weeks and returned with no constructive feedback on our test cases.
Rigorous course, but the professor broke down time complexity analysis brilliantly.
Anxiety-inducing quizzes with impossible 10-minute time limits for complex tree traversals.
Midterm exam questions were completely different from any practice problems provided.
Very rewarding course. The weekly algorithmic challenges pushed my problem solving skills.
The automated grading server kept crashing right before the submission deadlines.
The professor took time to explain geometric intuition behind eigenvectors. Fantastic lecture style.
Dry lecture delivery with virtually no real-world engineering applications discussed.
I felt lost during the second half of the course when we started vector spaces.
The textbook homework was repetitive and felt like high school busywork.
Clear chalkboard lectures and very well structured problem sets each Friday.
The syllabus suddenly changed halfway through the semester and grading criteria became totally confusing.
Unclear what topics will be tested on the final exam. The study guide is too generic.
Questions on the calculus exam were unfairly difficult and never covered in lectures.
Excellent review sessions before every exam, helped me boost my confidence.
Loved the laboratory experiments and visual demonstrations of rotational dynamics.
Lab equipment was outdated and broken sensors ruined our experimental measurements.
Continuous weekly lab reports on top of heavy problem sets caused unnecessary sleep deprivation.
The instructor has great passion for physics and always answers student questions patiently.
Three-hour afternoon lecture with zero breaks made it almost impossible to stay awake.
Lab manuals were full of typos and vague procedures that confused everyone in my cohort.
The professor ignored hands raised in the lecture hall and seemed annoyed when asked for clarification.
Unreasonable deduction of marks for minor formatting mistakes on the report cover page.
Formula sheets provided during exams were helpful and reduced unnecessary memorization stress.
Practical feedback on resume writing and research presentation slides was extremely valuable.
Felt like reading textbook chapters verbatim off PowerPoint slides with little engagement.
Group project members vanished and the instructor refused to take action on our peer evaluation.
Interactive mock interview sessions were both fun and prepared me for real job interviews.
The course content felt outdated and disconnected from modern engineering communication practices.
Constructive writing rubrics helped me dramatically improve my technical report writing.
Deadline announcements kept shifting at the last minute with zero email notice.
Energetic discussions and helpful peer-review workshops every Thursday.
The weekly programming quizzes gave quick feedback on what concepts I needed to review.
The balance between algorithmic proofs and practical coding implementations was spot on.
The professor's office hours were crowded, but they made sure every student's doubts were cleared.
Felt overwhelmed trying to complete twenty complex multi-variable calculus physics problems in two days.
The presentation skills I learned in this class directly helped me present my capstone project.
Stressful semester overall, but learning dynamic programming and graph traversals was very satisfying.
